standard_text: Simple machines (lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane, wedge and screw) and where we use them; friction; things that work with and without electricity; how a hand pump, bicycle, matka and solar cooker work; using electricity safely (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 7).

key_sub: Levers, pulleys, wheels and slopes help us move loads.
body_html:
How to think about it

Machines make work easier. Simple machines have few parts: a lever (see-saw, scissors) turns on a point called the fulcrum; a pulley (well) lets us pull down to lift up; a wheel and axle (cart) rolls loads; an inclined plane (ramp) lets us push loads up a slope; a wedge (axe) splits; a screw holds tightly.

Friction slows things that rub; oil reduces it, brakes use it. Some things need electricity (fan, bulb, mixer), others do not (bicycle, hand pump). Never touch switches with wet hands, and switch off lights and fans to save electricity.

Example

A see-saw is…

it turns about the middle

Answer: a lever

Example

Why use a ramp?

less effort

Answer: an inclined plane makes lifting easier

Common mistakes

  • Calling every machine with a wheel 'electric'.
  • Thinking friction is always bad.
  • Touching switches with wet hands.

faq.q: Why does a matka cool water?
